claim: The Park Service report says the Leister House served as headquarters for Union General George Meade on July 2 and 3 and was used as a hospital after fighting ceased on July 3.

source.edition: Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Military Park: Record of Treatment, Volume I (Areas 1-10) (2018)

quote: The Leister House served as the headquarters for Union General George Meade on July 2 and 3 and was used as a hospital after fighting ceased on July 3.

claim: The Park Service inventory says the area around the Trostle barn served as headquarters for Union General Daniel Sickles and the farmhouse was used briefly as a hospital.

source.edition: Cultural Landscapes Inventory: Emmitsburg Road Ridge Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park (2024)

quote: The area around the Trostle barn, located along Trostle Farm Lane, served as a headquarters for Union General Daniel Sickles and the farmhouse was used briefly as a hospital.

claim: The Park Service inventory says the Sherfy barn had been used as a shelter for wounded Union soldiers, many of whom died in the ensuing fire that consumed the barn.

source.edition: Cultural Landscapes Inventory: Pickett's Charge Battlefield, Gettysburg National Military Park (2024)
source.part: Joseph Sherfy Farm: Barn, Pickett's Charge Battlefield inventory (PDF p. 97)

quote: It had been used as a shelter for wounded Union soldiers, many of whom died in the ensuing fire that consumed the barn.

scene.may_show: Wounded Union soldiers sheltered in the Sherfy barn when the fire consumes it; documented by the Park Service, the number and the hour are not stated.
